questions.stem: Prove that a function f:ℝ→ℝ with f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) for all x,y, that is also monotonic (or bounded on an interval), must be f(x)=cx.

hint.level_1: Use a regularity condition to extend to reals.

solution_steps: From additivity, f(qx)=qf(x) for rationals q, so f(q)=cq with c=f(1).
Monotonicity (or local boundedness) forces f to agree with the linear map on all reals by density of ℚ.
questions.solution: From additivity, f(qx)=qf(x) for rationals q, so f(q)=cq with c=f(1). Monotonicity (or local boundedness) forces f to agree with the linear map on all reals by density of ℚ. Hence f(x)=cx.

questions.stem: Prove that a² + b² + c² ≥ ab + bc + ca for all reals.
solution_steps: Dividing by 2 gives a²+b²+c² ≥ ab+bc+ca, equality iff a=b=c.
questions.solution: Consider 2(a²+b²+c²) − 2(ab+bc+ca). This equals (a−b)² + (b−c)² + (c−a)² ≥ 0. Dividing by 2 gives a²+b²+c² ≥ ab+bc+ca, equality iff a=b=c.

solution_steps: The product telescopes: numerators and denominators cancel across consecutive terms.
questions.solution: 1 − 1/k² = (k−1)(k+1)/k². The product telescopes: numerators and denominators cancel across consecutive terms. What remains is (1·(n+1))/(2·n) = (n+1)/(2n).

questions.stem: Prove for positive reals a, b that 2/(1/a+1/b) ≤ √(ab) ≤ (a+b)/2.

hint.level_1: Apply AM–GM to the reciprocals for HM ≤ GM.

questions.solution: AM–GM gives (a+b)/2 ≥ √(ab). Apply AM–GM to 1/a, 1/b: (1/a+1/b)/2 ≥ 1/√(ab), i.e. √(ab) ≥ 2/(1/a+1/b). Combining gives HM ≤ GM ≤ AM.
questions.theme: Inequality of the means (HM ≤ GM ≤ AM)

questions.stem: State and prove Abel's summation formula Σ_{k=1}^{n} aₖbₖ = Aₙbₙ − Σ_{k=1}^{n−1} Aₖ(b_{k+1}−bₖ), where Aₖ = a₁+⋯+aₖ.

hint.level_0: Write aₖ as a difference of partial sums.

solution_steps: Substitute and regroup the sum by the bₖ, shifting indices.
The rearrangement yields Aₙbₙ − Σ Aₖ(b_{k+1}−bₖ) (a discrete integration by parts).
questions.solution: Write aₖ = Aₖ − A_{k−1} (with A₀=0). Substitute and regroup the sum by the bₖ, shifting indices. The rearrangement yields Aₙbₙ − Σ Aₖ(b_{k+1}−bₖ) (a discrete integration by parts).

questions.stem: State Descartes' Rule of Signs and use it to bound the number of positive real roots of x³ − 3x² + 2x − 5.

hint.level_0: Count sign changes of the coefficients.
hint.level_1: Subtract an even number for the possibilities.

solution_steps: Descartes: the number of positive real roots equals the number of sign changes in the coefficients, or less by an even number.
Coefficients +,−,+,− have 3 sign changes, so there are 3 or 1 positive real roots.
(Here exactly one, as a graph confirms.)

questions.stem: Prove the polynomial remainder theorem: the remainder of P(x) on division by (x−a) is P(a).
solution_steps: Write P(x) = (x−a)Q(x) + R, where the remainder R is a constant (degree < 1).
Substitute x = a: the first term vanishes.
questions.solution: Write P(x) = (x−a)Q(x) + R, where the remainder R is a constant (degree < 1). Substitute x = a: the first term vanishes. So R = P(a).

questions.stem: Evaluate 1² + 2² + ⋯ + 20².
Evaluate 1 + 3 + 5 + ⋯ + 29 (the first 15 odd numbers).

hint.level_0: Odd numbers sum to a perfect square.
hint.level_1: It is n² for the first n.

solution_steps: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n².
questions.solution: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². Here n = 15. So the sum is 15² = 225.

questions.stem: If a + b + c = 6 and ab + bc + ca = 11, find a² + b² + c².
Evaluate 2 + 6 + 18 + ⋯ + 2·3⁷.
solution_steps: Geometric: first term 2, ratio 3, eight terms.
questions.solution: Geometric: first term 2, ratio 3, eight terms. Sum = 2(3⁸ − 1)/(3 − 1) = 3⁸ − 1. = 6560.

questions.stem: Minimize x² + y² + z² subject to x + y + z = 9 (reals).
questions.solution: By Cauchy–Schwarz, 3(x²+y²+z²) ≥ (x+y+z)² = 81. So x²+y²+z² ≥ 27. Equality at x = y = z = 3.

questions.stem: Evaluate 2 + 4 + 6 + ⋯ + 100.
Find all real x with |x − 2| + |x + 3| = 7.

hint.level_0: Read it as a sum of two distances.

solution_steps: |x − 2| + |x + 3| is the total distance from x to 2 and to −3; its minimum is 5, attained for −3 ≤ x ≤ 2.
To reach 7 we need 2 more, which happens outside that interval.
Solving the cases x > 2 and x < −3 gives x = 3 and x = −4.

questions.stem: If x + 1/x = 5, find x⁴ + 1/x⁴.
Evaluate Σ_{k=1}^{10} 1/2ᵏ.
solution_steps: Geometric with first term 1/2, ratio 1/2, ten terms.
questions.solution: Geometric with first term 1/2, ratio 1/2, ten terms. Sum = (1/2)(1 − (1/2)¹⁰)/(1 − 1/2) = 1 − 1/1024. = 1023/1024.
